newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI Hetman 1996 net loss worse after audit.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI Hetman 1996 net loss worse after audit.

text.p: National Investment Fund Hetman (No 15) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme made a 1996 net loss of 102.9 million zlotys and not the previously reported 92.9 million, the fund's president said after a fund audit.

"At the end of 1996 the loss of the fund amounted to 102.9 million zlotys. That loss was influenced by a lowering of the results of firms...caused by the making of provisions," Krzysztof Sedzikowski told a news conference on Wednesday.
Sedzikowski said that such provisions were made at more firms than previously, adding that provisions made by the fund in 1996 amounted to 39.5 percent of the fund's net loss, or 35.9 million zlotys.
He said the 1996 restructuring costs of firms in the fund's portfolio were at about 50 million zlotys.
"That's an excellent investment," he said, referring to the restructuring costs and adding that the firm made a net profit of 0.7 million zlotys in this year's first quarter.

Sedzikowski said that during the first quarter the fund invested 32 million zlotys to take up shares in new issues by two of the firms in which it holds a strategic stake, chipboard maker Grajewo and cement firm Rudniki.
He said the fund spent another 4.4 million zlotys in new issues by four firms in which it has a minority stake.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control last year of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-size companies.
Each fund, run by international consortia of managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equities in the remaining firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme are entitled to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse as early as mid-June.
Sedzikowski also said the firm had opened two credit lines worth a total of 43 million zlotys, of which about 13.3 million zlotys had been used by the end of the first quarter.
